placement.content:
- **2026-10-12 — `fgctl init` downloads by default (RUL15 (fgctl init downloads a checksum-verified release when no source is given)).** Before this, a plain `fgctl init` in a project with no pin failed with "`--from <source>` is required", so a first install meant downloading the release tarball by hand. Owner decision: no source and no pin means the latest GitHub release; `FGCTL_VERSION` selects an exact tag; `FGCTL_FROM` and `--from` select a non-release build; checksum verification is mandatory; the transport is the system `curl` rather than a new HTTP crate (same behavior and override as `install.sh`, no TLS stack to carry in `fgctl`). Prior art: `fgctl init --from` (the release-asset door, kept unchanged and now equivalent to `FGCTL_FROM`), `install.sh`'s `FGCTL_VERSION`/`FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL`/`FGCTL_TARGET` (reused, not redefined). Same day, follow-up: the pin now records the tag, so a pinned workspace whose release is not staged on this machine downloads it instead of needing a source; only a digest-only legacy pin still needs `FGCTL_FROM`/`FGCTL_VERSION`/`--from`, because a digest names no download. Follow-up (2026-10-14): `fgctl upgrade` uses the same verified download pipeline (`--from` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION` > latest GitHub release) and records the downloaded tag in `.fgos/distribution.json`, so an upgraded project's pin keeps a downloadable `releaseVersion` for teammates instead of reverting to digest-only.
- **2026-10-13 — Windows is a native release target (RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell)).** Owner decision: the level is "native, complete" (PowerShell and `cmd.exe`, no Git Bash, no WSL), with `tar.gz` kept as the single archive format and macOS left out of scope. Prior art, reused: the Windows CI hardening track made the Rust workspace build and the release-tree staging work on Windows (the `fgos.exe` entry, colon-free release store directory names, drive-letter-safe archive validation), and an earlier change wrote `.cmd` launchers on Windows that ran the `sh` shims through a `sh` on `PATH`; that required Git for Windows, so it is replaced by launchers that read `activation.json` themselves. Missing before: a Windows release asset, `install.ps1`, a Windows consumer proof, and any check that the launchers exist. Also in this change: the Linux asset moves from `ubuntu-latest` (binaries then needed glibc 2.39 and printed a loader warning on Ubuntu 22.04, glibc 2.35) to `ubuntu-22.04`, with a CI gate on the glibc symbol versions.
- **2026-10-16 — fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; YAML is read through one vendored parser (RUL101 (fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml 5.4.3 behind src/util/yaml.mjs)).** Before this, `yaml` was the one production dependency. An installed release carried it (the release builder stages declared production dependencies), but a checkout, linked worktree or unpacked copy without `npm install` did not, so every module importing it failed to load there, and the doctor and setup paths grew their own YAML readers and "not evaluated" branches to keep loading. Decision: `package.json#dependencies` stays empty; the only YAML parser is `src/util/third-party/js-yaml.mjs`, the ESM bundle from the js-yaml 5.4.3 tarball, unmodified except a header and the dropped source-map comment line, and every parse goes through `src/util/yaml.mjs` (`parseYaml(text, { filename })`: zero documents give `null`, more than one throws, `maxAliases` 100, js-yaml's default core schema). An architecture test fails on any other import of `yaml`, `js-yaml` or the third-party file. Rejected: keeping `yaml` and making doctor tolerate its absence (what the workarounds did, and the cause of the divergence); a hand-rolled parser (a second authority for what YAML means); `vendor/` or `dist/` as the location (the repository's scout-block hook refuses those path segments, so agents could not read or review the file); 5.4.2 (a block-indentation mis-parse fixed in 5.4.3) and 5.5.0 (one day old at the time). Readers that used to skip silently now report a parse failure as a named problem with file, line and column; pinned persona text that the strict parser rejects renders through a private legacy projection so older runs resume with the same text (its removal is tracked in the backlog). Evidence: commits `8ef1baf1c` (door and vendored file), `838b044e5` (call sites), `b75c01a3f` (release and dev-host staging), `6013ca389` (dependency dropped), `f96eece77`, `b7eeb4bb6` and `26b3338a7` (readers use the parser), `f705b9c8c` (doctor checks `compiled.json`); a parity run of the old parser against the door over every tracked YAML and frontmatter document found 828 documents, 0 differences, 13 rejected by both; a cold `fgos` start costs 2 to 3 ms more (97 to 99 ms for `version`, 109 to 110 ms for `dispatch decide`); the full suite ran 7850 tests with 0 failures with release binaries present; `test/util/yaml.test.mjs` pins the vendored bytes by hash. Kept on their own paths: `src/report/frontmatter.mjs` pairs `parseFrontmatter` with `renderFrontmatter` over a deliberately flat schema, so replacing only the parser would make the pair asymmetric; `distill.mjs` carries a minimal YAML reader because portable skills ship without `src/`; `domains/*/compiled.json` stays a generated projection because parsing domain YAML at import would put every verb, hook and `doctor` at the mercy of one YAML typo (doctor now checks its freshness instead). Upgrade procedure: in an empty scratch directory run `npm pack js-yaml@<version> --ignore-scripts`; compare the tarball's sha512 with `npm view js-yaml@<version> dist.integrity`; extract the `.mjs` bundle from the tarball without executing anything in it (build the path so the hook-refused segment does not appear in the command); confirm it has no import or require; diff it against the current bundle and read every changed line; re-run the parity comparison against the previous parser over the tracked YAML; replace the third-party file with the new bundle under a fresh header (source, version, integrity, license, hash); update the hash constant in `test/util/yaml.test.mjs`. js-yaml advisories are watched through the backlog, since `npm audit` no longer covers the file.
- **2026-10-17 — Instruction composition belongs to the Agent Context Engine; packaging-distribution delivers (RUL102 (one owner for composing agent instructions: the Agent Context Engine composes and selects rules, packaging-distribution only discovers, installs, renders per host and repairs)).** Before this, two documents gave the same authority to two components: `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/contracts/instruction-composition-and-projection.md` §2 named packaging-distribution owner of the composition engine and registry shape, while `docs/platform/proposals/documentation-system-unification.md` §4.7.2-4.7.3 put the Instruction Composer in the Agent Context Engine and said packaging-distribution "does not decide semantic composition". Left as is, a future Agent Context Engine would be built beside `src/setup/instruction-composition.mjs`, giving two composers and two orderings of the same rules. Owner decision: composing and selecting rules (kind order, override, conflict, per-task selection, per-host budget, progressive disclosure) has one owner, the Agent Context Engine; packaging-distribution keeps delivery (source discovery and install, per-host render adapters, projection ledger, doctor repair). Two delivery moments follow: static delivery, where packaging-distribution asks the engine for each host's effective set when sources change or at setup/install/upgrade and renders it to files; and per-task delivery, where the runner asks the engine for a context packet that goes into the worker brief, with no file written. The engine knows no host or file. Rejected: packaging-distribution keeping composition and also absorbing budgets and per-task selection (it would grow a content-deciding role inside an install/delivery component). Weight guard: no new component now; the existing code in `src/setup/instruction-registry.mjs` and `src/setup/instruction-composition.mjs` is the engine's seed and moves to its own module only when the first budget/tiering slice lands, in the same change, never kept in two places. Evidence and reasoning: `plans/reports/research-261016-1118-agent-code-quality-guardrails.md` sections 2d and 6.

An architecture test fails on any other import of `yaml`, `js-yaml` or the third-party file. Rejected: keeping `yaml` and making doctor tolerate its absence (what the workarounds did, and the cause of the divergence); a hand-rolled parser (a second authority for what YAML means); `vendor/` or `dist/` as the location (the repository's scout-block hook refuses those path segments, so agents could not read or review the file); 5.4.2 (a block-indentation mis-parse fixed in 5.4.3) and 5.5.0 (one day old at the time). Readers that used to skip silently now report a parse failure as a named problem with file, line and column; pinned persona text that the strict parser rejects renders through a private legacy projection so older runs resume with the same text (its removal is tracked in the backlog). - A package marked as not intended for public registry publication can still
  be installed directly from its GitHub repository — that restriction only
  blocks publishing to a public registry, not this installation path.
- Both CLI entry points (`fgos` and `fgos-runner`) are installed identically,
  executable immediately after install — a fresh install does not require
  the installer to separately locate or make executable the autonomous-loop
  runner command.
- Calling `fgos`/`fgos-runner` (via the dev checkout shell helper) from
  inside a linked git worktree of this repository always runs the MAIN
  checkout's entry point, never that worktree's own local copy — accepted
  as-is for this mechanism, not treated as a defect.
- A package manager whose own policy blocks lifecycle scripts for
  git-hosted dependencies (e.g. pnpm 10+'s `allowBuilds`) never blocks
  installing this package, because this package's install never declares a
  lifecycle script in the first place (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle) —
  there is nothing for that policy to approve or refuse.
- `fgos setup` run a second time with nothing new to do reports that
  plainly rather than silently repeating (or silently no-oping without
  saying so).
- `fgos doctor`'s `config-not-stale` check on a machine where `fgos setup`
  was never run reports "not configured yet", not an error and not a
  silently-created file.
- A release tree staged for `fgctl` (`scripts/build-rust-distribution.mjs`)
  carries the legacy-node payload TOGETHER WITH its production dependencies
  (the package's `dependencies` and theirs), copied next to the sources, so
  every verb runs from the installed release alone. Before this, the staged
  tree held no dependencies and any verb that loads one (`fgos workflow`,
  found when dogfooding a project that had run `fgctl init`) failed with a
  missing-package error while `fgos version` and `fgos doctor` still passed.
  A dependency that is not installed when the tree is built fails the build
  instead of thinning the payload; two installed copies of one name are
  refused. The external-consumer CI step runs a dependency-loading verb for
  this reason, because `version` never imports one.
- An agent in a project with no `bin/` (only the installed `fgos`) finds how
  to run anything from `fgos --help --json` and `fgos <verb> [<sub>] --help
  --json`. The host's route table carries two option selectors, `--help` and
  `-h`, generated from `HELP_SELECTORS` in `src/cli/command-registry.mjs`
  like every verb route and sent to the legacy-node payload, which owns the
  verb manifest; every other leading option still has no route and exits 4.
  A Rust-native verb given an exact `--help`/`-h` token anywhere after it is
  sent to the payload too, so it prints its manifest entry instead of
  running. `fgos version` lists verbs only, never the two help selectors.

   lạ tự tìm được việc kế tiếp từ chính state của forgent.

placement.content:
- **fgOS mô hình hoá quan hệ giữa các work item bằng MỘT đồ thị cạnh-định-kiểu
  DẪN XUẤT** (derived — không phải một trường vật lý mới): `deps` chiếu thành
  cạnh `blocks` (`I -> d`, nghĩa "I chờ d"); `parent` chiếu thành cạnh
  `parent-child` (`P -> C`, nghĩa "cha chờ con" — đúng hướng
  `hasOpenDescendant` của `frontier.mjs`, không phải hướng con→cha ngây thơ,
  vì hướng ngây thơ sẽ làm một chu trình hỗn hợp blocks/parent-child không
  phát hiện được). `waits-for` và `discovered-from` là **từ vựng đã khai báo**
  — chưa có dạng lưu trữ hay producer nào (hoãn sang S2b).
- **Quyết định này SUPERSEDE 0002** (và spec Data Dictionary #13,
  `work.mjs:164-166`) ở đúng một điểm: "deps và parent tách rời có chủ đích"
  giờ đọc là "tách rời về **lưu trữ và ngữ nghĩa**, nhưng hợp nhất thành
  **một đồ thị** cho cycle-check và mọi compute slice sau này (S5+)". 0002
  không sai về lưu trữ — phần đó giữ nguyên; nó chỉ chưa tính tới việc hai
  quan hệ cần chung một bảo đảm phi-chu-trình.
- **Bảo đảm phi-chu-trình tại cửa ghi duy nhất (`store.mjs`) giờ phủ ĐỒ THỊ
  HỢP NHẤT `blocks`+`parent-child`**, không chỉ `deps` — **đã ship và verify
  xanh** (work-graph-intelligence cell -3/-4): `src/state/dep-graph.mjs` thêm
  `buildUnifiedEdges`/`findUnifiedCycle`/`assertNoUnifiedCycle` bên cạnh các
  hàm `deps`-only của S1 (`findDepCycle`/`assertNoCycle`, giữ nguyên hành vi
  và chữ ký); `store.mjs` gọi `assertNoUnifiedCycle` cạnh `assertNoCycle` cũ
  tại cả `addWork` và `editWork`, trước `appendEvent`. Điều này **đóng** lỗ
  hổng chu trình cha-con sống nói trên (benign nhưng có thật) — làm cho bất
  biến 896219a7 ("đồ thị phi chu trình") đúng cho **toàn bộ** đồ thị hợp
  nhất, không chỉ nhánh `deps`.
- **Dẫn xuất, không vật lý (derived-not-physical) — ba căn cứ:**
  1. **RUL11 (tiến hóa schema)** (log bất khả xâm phạm, `work-state.md:703`): một trường
     `edges[]` lưu trữ mới sẽ đòi migration cho mọi event cũ; một
     read-projection thuần Domain thì không.
  2. **Học thuyết DT2 "add-through-không-alongside"**: mở rộng cửa ghi hiện
     có (`assertNoCycle` cộng thêm `assertNoUnifiedCycle`, cùng một cửa)
     thay vì mở một đường ghi song song.
  3. **~10 consumer đọc trực tiếp `.deps`/`.parent`** (frontier, impact,
     `validateDeps`, v.v.) — giữ nguyên, không cần migrate.
- Vì thuần dẫn xuất: **không có trường lưu trữ mới; tại thời điểm quyết định
  này, SCHEMA_VERSION vẫn ở 2** (nay đã lên 3, per str46-io-contract),
  mọi event cũ replay y hệt (RUL11 (tiến hóa schema)).

`title`/`description` trong một khối `fgos-discovered` là VĂN BẢN KHÔNG ĐÁNG TIN — do
chính worker (một trợ lý đang chạy, có thể bị chèn lệnh từ nội dung không đáng tin nó
đọc phải) tự soạn. Item runner tạo ra từ đó vào thẳng giai đoạn `clarify`, nơi
`title`/`description` nạp vào prompt của MODEL làm-rõ — đây là mặt tiếp xúc thứ hai
(sau chính worker) nơi văn bản không đáng tin chạm tới một model sẽ sinh ra lệnh chạy
được. Chấp nhận CÓ CHỦ Ý, không phải bỏ sót: giảm nhẹ đã có từ thiết kế gốc giữ nguyên
— `verify` KHÔNG BAO GIỜ do worker đặt (luôn `FALLBACK_VERIFY` rồi model/người ở bước
làm-rõ gán lại), nên văn bản worker không đáng tin không thể trực tiếp trở thành một
lệnh shell chạy được; item không mang niềm tin đặc biệt nào, đi qua đúng vòng xét-lại
như một item người tự khai. **Phương án đã cân nhắc, CHƯA XÂY:** một cửa xét-duyệt-người
bắt buộc trước khi một item runner-tự-tạo được dispatch tự động (thay vì vào thẳng
`clarify` như hôm nay) — đổi thiết kế lớn hơn phạm vi một P3 review-fix, ghi lại đây để
cân nhắc lại nếu bằng chứng chèn-lệnh thật xuất hiện.

placement.content:
- **Phạm vi (coverage).** Miễn trừ bao trùm cả BA kho `.fgos` liệt ở trên: kho
  sống dùng chung, kho `dogfood-fixture`, và kho `fgos-test-drive`. Cả ba cùng
  nằm trong phạm vi được phép viết lại — không phân biệt kho nào "quan trọng
  hơn" kho nào.
- **Lát cắt (slicing) là chuyện khác, tách bạch khỏi phạm vi.** Slice nào của
  STR46 thực sự thi hành việc viết lại cho kho nào là một quyết định lịch trình,
  không phải một quyết định phạm vi, và nó đã bị dời hai lần: kho sống được dời
  sang bước merge (vì nó dùng chung qua symlink giữa mọi worktree đang sống, và
  viết lại lúc mã còn trên nhánh chưa merge sẽ mở cửa sổ hỏng), rồi kho
  `fgos-test-drive` theo sau khi write-guard được đo là từ chối mọi đường dẫn nằm
  ngoài worktree. Một bản ghi vĩnh viễn không được kế thừa một quyết định lịch
  trình còn đang di chuyển — nên bản ghi này chỉ khoá PHẠM VI, không khoá SLICE
  nào viết kho nào lúc nào.
- **Hết hiệu lực (lapse).** Miễn trừ này **hết hiệu lực khi sản phẩm lên
  v1.0.0**. Từ mốc đó, `RUL11 (tiến hóa schema)` áp dụng đầy đủ trở lại không ngoại lệ — không có
  mốc thì "đang còn xây" sẽ thành một cái cớ vĩnh viễn.
- **Không bao gồm.** Miễn trừ này **không** bao trùm
  `repo/test/fixtures/phase1-events.jsonl` — file đã commit, header tự khai
  "NEVER regenerated or hand-edited", và mang một khẳng định bất biến riêng tại
  `test/state/backward-compat.test.mjs:245` ("the fixture file itself is never
  modified by any test in this suite"). File này không mang trường `actor` nên
  không có gì để đổi; nó bị loại rõ ràng để một script quét theo mẫu
  `**/events.jsonl` không vô tình chạm vào nó.

placement.content:
**Luật gốc (nguyên văn từ `work-state.md` dòng 1070, RUL35 (domain — chiều thứ ba chi phối bộ stage, song song status/stage)):** "Một
domain khai đúng ba thứ: danh sách stage có thứ tự, step-mapping (bước nào
trong 5 bước base-workflow mỗi stage thỏa), và cạnh chuyển-stage hợp lệ riêng
của nó — domain KHÔNG BAO GIỜ chi phối bảng chuyển-status (`fsm.mjs`), tách
bạch tuyệt đối khỏi `status`." Nói cách khác: `stage` (vĩ mô — domain tự khai
qua `DOMAINS` registry, `workflow-stage-graphs.mjs`) và `status` (vi mô — một
bảng `TRANSITIONS` PHẲNG duy nhất trong `status-fsm.mjs`, dùng chung cho MỌI
domain, không domain nào override) là hai trục tách biệt tuyệt đối. Domain
`coding` và `synthetic` hôm nay (`workflow-stage-graphs.mjs` dòng 51-91) đúng
là ví dụ sống của vế đầu (`DOMAINS[domain].stages/stepMap/transitions`); vế
sau (status) chưa từng có tương đương — `status-fsm.mjs`'s `TRANSITIONS`
(24 cạnh) và `work.mjs`'s `STATUSES` (10 giá trị: `todo`/`doing`/`blocked`/
`awaiting-approval`/`awaiting-human`/`delivered`/`retrospective`/`cleanup`/
`done`/`wontfix`) là hằng số toàn cục duy nhất, không tham số hoá theo
`work.domain` ở đâu cả.

- **NHÓM ĐẦU — 6 status TRƯỚC `delivered`:** `todo` / `doing` / `blocked` /
  `awaiting-human` / `awaiting-approval` / `wontfix`. Kể từ record này, domain
  SỞ HỮU nhãn + bảng transition riêng cho nhóm này — đây là phần thật sự
  supersede `base-workflow-model`. Domain KHÔNG BẮT BUỘC đổi tên
  (coding giữ nguyên cả 6 chữ, 0 migration) — cả hai điều này chỉ trao QUYỀN, không
  ép dùng.
- **NHÓM ĐUÔI — 4 status TỪ `delivered` trở đi:** `delivered` → `retrospective`
  → `cleanup` → `done`, chuỗi TUYẾN TÍNH cố định. KHÔNG domain nào được
  relabel — đây là nghĩa vụ phổ quát của bất kỳ loại hình việc nào (delivery
  thật, nhìn lại, dọn dẹp), không phải từ vựng riêng của `coding` (xác
  nhận trực tiếp: "loại hình việc nào cũng cần delivery, retro, và cleanup...
  chỉ có tổ chức nào quá hời hợt sẽ bỏ qua retro và cleanup"). Khác biệt
  per-domain ở nhóm này nằm ở **skill nào chạy** bước `retrospective` (mở
  rộng đúng field `skillMap` đã có trong `DOMAINS[domain]`,
  `workflow-stage-graphs.mjs`, thêm key `retrospective`; `cleanup` giữ nguyên
  pure-harness, không cần skill — khác biệt per-domain của nó đã đủ qua field
  `worktreeBacked` có sẵn), KHÔNG phải ở tên/cạnh chuyển status.

domain.

Quét bằng `rg -n "STATUSES|TRANSITIONS" src/ bin/ --glob '*.mjs'` và
`rg -n "'todo'|'doing'|'blocked'|'awaiting-approval'|'awaiting-human'|
'delivered'|'retrospective'|'cleanup'|'wontfix'"` trên `frontier.mjs`,
`retro-pool.mjs`, `status-fsm.mjs`, `runner/*.mjs`, `bin/fgos.mjs` — cộng thêm
quét mở rộng ra mọi consumer thật của tập `RESOLVED_STATUSES` (đã là 1 tập
"giống category" viết tay, DISCUSSION.md §3 #3) và ra khỏi thư mục `src/`/`bin/`
(CLI-display doc, external Rust consumer) để không bỏ sót theo đúng yêu cầu
acceptance của `tsk-38t`. Cột "Đổi?" nói rõ consumer này có cần đổi sang đọc
`statusCategory` (hoặc bảng transition riêng của domain) hay giữ nguyên literal
mãi mãi theo đúng ranh giới đầu/đuôi vừa chốt ở trên.

placement.content:
- **Record này là tiền điều kiện bắt buộc cho `tsk-38t-2` đến `tsk-38t-7`**
  (schema `statusCategory`/`STATUS_CATEGORIES`, migration backfill,
  consumer-migration theo audit ở trên, `skillMap.retrospective`,
  `domainFields`/`fieldSchema`, domain giả lập thứ hai THẬT có bảng
  transition khác coding để chứng minh thiết kế) — **không phần nào trong số
  đó được bắt đầu code trước khi file này tồn tại**, đúng yêu cầu acceptance
  gốc của `tsk-38t` ("cần decision record mới đúng khuôn 0024 supersede 0006,
  viết TRƯỚC khi code").
- `base-workflow-model` (`2ae492d8`) KHÔNG bị sửa tại chỗ — nguyên văn
  của nó vẫn đúng lịch sử; record này chỉ supersede đúng phạm vi status/domain
  đã nêu, không phải toàn bộ ngữ cảnh `base-workflow-model` (S1/S2 domain
  registry cho `stage` vẫn đứng nguyên, không bị chạm).
- `RESOLVED_STATUSES` (`frontier.mjs:186`) và mọi consumer của nó (§2 ở trên)
  là điểm rủi ro tập trung nhất khi hiện thực hoá — nó là tập string viết tay
  DUY NHẤT hôm nay trộn cả 2 nhóm đầu/đuôi; sửa sai chỗ này lan ra ít nhất 7
  file khác (`graph-metrics.mjs`, `graph-harness.mjs`, `drift-status.mjs`,
  `impact.mjs`, `claim-port.mjs`, `entropy.mjs`, `bin/fgos.mjs`) chỉ vì chúng
  gọi `.has` trên đúng 1 Set dùng chung.
  `entropy.mjs`/`bin/fgos.mjs`'s `FINAL_STATUSES` cục bộ là 2 bản sao ĐÃ LỆCH
  nghĩa nhau (khác tập con) — cần rà đồng thời, không chỉ theo dấu
  `RESOLVED_STATUSES`.
- `packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust/src/fgos.rs` xác nhận việc audit "consumer của status" không
  dừng ở biên `src/`/`bin/` của repo Node — bất kỳ tiến trình ngoài nào đọc
  `fgos list --all --json` cũng là 1 consumer thật của vocabulary status, cần
  đưa vào phạm vi khi `tsk-38t-3` (consumer-migration) thực thi.
- `docs/reference/triage-table-columns.md` lệch code (7 vs 10 status thật) là
  gap có thật nhưng ĐỘC LẬP khỏi quyết định category — không chặn record này,
  nhưng nên sửa cùng đợt `tsk-38t-3` để tránh phải quét lại 2 lần.

  thật vào event log + đánh thức đúng vai — *không bao giờ phán đoán*.
  Soul (agent-type) hiểu vai trò, hiểu vấn đề, biết cần ai support — *tự
  chọn* edge hợp lệ. Route bậy → REFUSED kèm danh sách edge hợp lệ
  (chặn và dạy tại chỗ).
- **Ba trục trực giao trên work item**: `status` (lifecycle phổ quát, 11
  trạng thái — giữ nguyên) × `stage` (thuộc workflow đã chọn) ×
  `role/holder` (mới, opt-in per-domain qua `roleGraph`).
- **Ba tầng điều phối không giẫm nhau**: Router/Driver (who/what-next —
  `fgos-routing`, `fgos-coding-driving`) / Guard (legality — FSM +
  roleGraph + gates) / Dispatch (executor nào chạy —
  `src/runner/dispatch.mjs` decide/execute, một cửa).

placement.content:
- **Hai loại handoff**: **Call** (round-trip, bóng về người gửi) với 4
  reason do người dùng định nghĩa: `advise` / `assist` (tay chân) /
  `review` (phản biện) / `consult` (chuyên môn) — tổng quát hoá
  `fgos ask/answer` sẵn có. **Pass** (chuyển giao một chiều theo stage).
  Ranh giới: cùng item → handoff; khác item/cây → signal.
- **Call lồng được, trần callstack** (mặc định 3, config override — con
  số cụ thể do planning quyết, người dùng chốt nguyên tắc vòng 5).
- **Ghi log hai mức**: async call = handoff event đầy đủ, holder
  đổi; sync call trong-session (subagent) = một event `call-summary`
  gọn, holder giữ nguyên. Invariant: *holder chỉ đổi qua async handoff*.
  Mỗi handoff = một checkpoint hạt mịn tự nhiên (context snapshot trong
  event + worktree commit cho artifact) — không cần checkpoint machinery
  riêng như cockpit.
- **Gate hard/soft**: hard một-chiều ⟺ side effect vượt ranh giới
  item/worktree (merge main CTR005, publish ra ngoài, terminal
  done/wontfix, cleanup đã xoá worktree; vùng hậu-merge một chiều —
  rework = item mới). Mọi gate nội bộ item = soft: quay lại được nhưng
  *bắt buộc ghi reason* → rework thành tín hiệu compound-learn. Áp
  nguyên xi cho marketing (publish = hard, editorial approval = soft).

placement.content:
- **Nối dây handoff thật**: 5 skill coding-domain (`fgos-coding-implement`/
  `discovering`/`exploring`/`planning`/`validating`) nối dây thật vào
  `handoff`/`handoff-return` — không chỉ có cơ chế, mà skill THẬT gọi nó.
- **Review độc lập**: review độc lập (agent `code-reviewer` mới, không chia sẻ
  context) tìm ra 2 lỗi HIGH + 3 MED + 4 LOW trong chính cách nối dây
  handoff thật vừa làm ở trên — tất cả đã sửa (chi tiết: giữ role/holder axis nhất quán qua
  reclaim lặp tới khi về `implementer`, `roleGraph` phủ cả stage
  `decompose` legacy, v.v.).
- **Khoá `kind` sau khi rời `todo`**: một câu hỏi kiến trúc của người dùng ("`fgos-coding-driving`
  có nên là cross-workflow router?") dẫn tới tư vấn Opus độc lập, phát
  hiện `kind` (field chọn workflow của item) sửa tự do không kiểm soát —
  fix: khoá `kind` một khi `status` rời `todo`, không cần field
  `workflow` riêng.
- **Chuyển lệnh review vào ENGINE**: một lần chạy AGENT THẬT (không phải test đơn vị) theo đúng
  prose của `fgos-coding-implement`, trên một item thật, phát hiện
  handoff `review` KHÔNG bắn được trong thực tế dù prose ra lệnh rõ ràng
  — nguyên nhân: lệnh nằm cuối, lặp lại 2 lần (return/catchup), không gì

| Entry point | Status | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `install.sh` | Implemented | Installs `fgctl` from release assets into a machine-local install directory. |
| `install.ps1` | Implemented preview | The Windows counterpart of `install.sh` (PowerShell 5.1 or later, no administrator rights, no `PATH` change): installs `fgctl.exe` for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` with the same `FGCTL_VERSION` / `FGCTL_INSTALL_DIR` / `FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL` / `FGCTL_TARGET` semantics and a mandatory `SHA256SUMS` check (rule RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell) in `docs/specs/distribution.md`). |
| `fgctl init` | Implemented preview | Initializes a project/workspace from a release chosen by `--from` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION` > the committed pin > the latest GitHub release; a downloaded asset is checksum-verified against `SHA256SUMS` before staging (rule RUL15 (fgctl init downloads a checksum-verified release when no source is given) in `docs/specs/distribution.md`). |
| `fgos` launcher | Implemented preview | One `fgos` (`fgos.cmd` on Windows) written next to `fgctl` by `fgos doctor --fix` (which `fgctl init` runs): it walks up to the nearest `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos` and runs it, so each project runs its own activated release with no absolute path and no rc edit. A different `fgos` found first on `PATH` is reported, never overwritten. See distribution spec RUL17 (one fgos on PATH runs each project's own activated fgos). |
| `fgctl upgrade` | Implemented preview | Moves a workspace activation to a new release chosen by `--from` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION` > the latest GitHub release (checksum-verified against `SHA256SUMS` when downloaded), records the previous release for rollback, and updates `.fgos/distribution.json` (including `releaseVersion` when downloaded). |
| `fgctl repair` | Implemented preview | Repairs a workspace installation under the selected release model; current preview proof covers repair after activation. |
| `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos` | Implemented preview | Stable workspace command surface after activation; current preview proof reports `host: "rust"` and the activated `artifactDigest`. |
| `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos.cmd`, `fgos-runner.cmd` | Implemented preview | The same stable surface for PowerShell and `cmd.exe`, written by `fgctl init`/`repair` next to the `sh` pair and needing no POSIX shell; `fgctl verify` reports a missing or edited launcher and `fgctl repair` regenerates it. |
| `npm install -g github:vantt/forgent` | Implemented legacy deprecated | Installs the legacy Node `fgos` and `fgos-runner` entry points; explicit deprecated escape hatch during the compatibility window, not the public/default posture. |
| `scripts/fgos-shell-integration.sh` | Implemented | Contributor/dev helper that resolves fgOS command tiers from shell functions. |
| local `fgos init` | Partial target | Adopts/materializes workspace state after `fgctl` publishes a ready activation. |
| `fgos doctor` | Implemented | Reports environment checks without writing by default. |
| `fgos doctor --fix` | Implemented | Runs registered fixes and then reports checks. |
| `fgos setup` | Implemented deprecated legacy compatibility | Wires local development support and runs registered environment repairs in the current Node CLI; command surfaces point workspace onboarding to `fgctl init` plus local `fgos doctor --fix`/`fgos doctor`, while shell/global integration remains compatibility behavior through the 30-day preview fallback window unless a later release decision replaces it. |

| Decision | Status |
|---|---|
| Runtime identity is digest-based, not PATH-based. | Settled for V1. |
| `artifactDigest` is the digest of the canonical release tree manifest, not an archive digest. | Settled for V1. |
| Release tree manifest uses normalized logical paths and refuses symlinks/case collisions in V1. | Settled for V1. |
| Project commands enter through stable local shims under workspace `.fgos/installation/bin/`. | Settled for V1. |
| Immutable release payloads live under a shared content-addressed machine/trust-domain release store, not under each worktree. | Settled for V1. |
| Activation is per workspace via `.fgos/installation/activation.json`; there is no single repository-wide active runtime pointer in V1. | Settled for V1. |
| Packaging release/activation state uses workspace installation roots and must not share a namespace with work coordination state. | Settled for V1. |
| The project/team pin is tracked as `.fgos/distribution.json`; machine-local activation state remains ignored. | Settled for V1. |
| `activation.json` is a durably published workspace binding, not a symlink, in V1. | Settled for V1. |
| Install transaction state lives under the release store root's `installs/<activationId>.json`, not inside `activation.json`. | Settled for V1. |
| Mutating invocations create lease files; `fgctl` may stage/verify during leases but refuses activation while a non-stale mutating lease exists. | Settled for V1. |
| V1 does not do automatic state migration during upgrade/rollback. | Settled for V1. |
| `fgctl` never writes host-visible projection files directly; local `fgos init` / `doctor --fix` owns projection materialization under active identity. | Settled for V1. |
| Existing projects are adoptable: a missing state schema record is treated as schema `1` and written during local `fgos init`. | Settled for V1. |
| Source checkouts support explicit `dev:<rev>` activation for dogfood; it is non-distributable and skips immutable release guarantees. | Selected V1 design conserved above; mechanism unimplemented, Plan C not a cutover prerequisite. |
| `fgctl` V1 is a Rust bootstrap binary with local path/tarball and GitHub release asset as acquisition sources. | Settled for V1. |
| Candidate preflight is static: `fgctl` never executes candidate release code before the ready binding is published. | Settled for V1 (P7 red-team fix, 2026-09-14). |
| Shared gateway/web are architecture constraints only, not active delivery scope. | Promoted for active delivery. |

| `MigrationJournal` | Append-only, project-local | local `fgos` under active identity | Records state-schema migration epoch, checkpoints/backups, reversibility, and compatibility facts. |

placement.content: `components.legacyNode` names a payload **root** plus an **entry** inside it, not a single file (proposed 2026-09-10 by the host-invocation stream, see [Legacy CLI Transition](../../host-invocation-routing/architecture/legacy-cli-transition.md) §2): the legacy payload is the whole Node package as `package.json` `files` defines it, staged with its source-relative layout intact so `bin/fgos.mjs` needs no import changes, and `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` lives in the same root. The Rust host resolves `join(activeReleasePath, root, entry)` and nothing else. A `dev:<rev>` source activation declares `root: "."`, `entry: "bin/fgos.mjs"`, `entries.fgos: "target/release/fgos"` — the same fields serve dogfood and a staged release.

placement.content:
| Field / Rule | V1 Decision |
|---|---|
| Path root | All paths are relative to the release root. Absolute paths are invalid. |
| Path separator | Always `/`, including on Windows. |
| Path normalization | UTF-8 NFC normalization before ordering and digesting. |
| Path order | Lexicographic byte order after normalization. |
| Case collision | Refuse a release if two paths collide under case-insensitive comparison. |
| File digest | SHA-256 of exact release-build bytes. |
| Line endings | Included in file bytes. Build must normalize if needed; install must not rewrite. |
| Executable bit | Included as `mode`, at least `755` vs `644`. |
| Directory entries | Not hashed as separate entries; directories are inferred from file paths. |
| Symlink | Refused in V1. Add explicit `kind: "symlink"` later only with relative, non-escaping targets. |
| mtime / owner / group | Excluded from runtime identity. |
| Archive digest | Optional `transportDigest`; never the runtime identity. |

placement.content:
Drift classes:

| Drift | Detector | Allowed Automatic Action |
|---|---|---|
| Immutable release file digest mismatch | `fgctl verify` or local `fgos doctor` reporting active identity | Quarantine/refuse. Do not patch individual release files. |
| Projection differs from generated baseline | local `fgos doctor` | `doctor --fix` may repair only when ownership and three-way comparison allow it. |
| Managed config differs from default | local `fgos doctor` | Schema-aware merge if registered as safe. |
| Mutable state/log/cache differs | N/A | Excluded from release drift. |

Plugin mirrors stay byte-identical to `.agents/skills/`, while Claude `SKILL.md` files are thin redirects with byte-identical frontmatter (`test/skills/fgos-mirror.test.mjs`). placement.content:
- **Blocked when:** never — running `fgos setup` always attempts its work;
  a shell profile that does not exist is simply skipped rather than
  refused.
- **What changes:** for every shell profile the caller actually has (bash's
  and/or zsh's, whichever exist), the shell helper's source line is added
  if not already present — never duplicated on a repeat run. The local
  project config file is also brought up to date: any setting present in
  the current default schema but missing from the caller's file is added,
  without ever changing a setting the caller already customized; a config
  file that already has every current default is left untouched. The same
  fill-missing-only treatment is applied to the **global** config file
  (`~/.fgos/config.json`, tsk-1ri) — `fgos setup` initializes it with the
  same default schema the project-local file gets, or fills in any missing
  key, every time it runs, regardless of which project it's run from;
  a value the caller already customized at the global level is never
  overwritten. The lock directories of row 5g are created when missing:
  `<lockRoot>` and `<fgosDir>/locks`, both mode 0700, an existing one tightened to it (the `lock-dirs` fix);
  the `terminal` section of row 5h is one of the defaults the
  fill-missing-only merge adds; `<stateRoot>/terminal` is created with mode 0700 (the
  `terminal-dir` fix).
- **Side effects:** the caller's own shell profile file(s), local project
  config file, global config file (`~/.fgos/config.json`), the two lock
  directories and `<stateRoot>/terminal` may be created or modified; nothing outside the caller's own
  environment is touched, and no network access happens.
- **Afterwards:** the caller sees exactly what changed — which profile
  file(s) gained the source line (or already had it), which project config
  settings were newly added (or that none were needed), and which global
  config settings were newly added (or that none were needed, or that the
  global file was just created). Nothing is done silently; running `fgos
  setup` again when everything is already current reports that plainly,
  without repeating any change.

- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The "trust vanishing" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself. - **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`; `no-confined-cli` when no probed invocation declares a sandbox). The verdict reads only the rows whose invocation declares its own sandbox (`confined: true`, each row's `inVerdict`): the read-only posture makes the door confine every round (`resolvePosture` returns a required `host-write-denied` requirement), and an invocation that declares no sandbox binds no private home either, so its CLI meets its own login directory (`CODEX_HOME`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) mounted read-only and stops on `EROFS` before it answers. That row is still run and reported (outcome `sandbox`, truthfully: a read-only dispatch pinned to that invocation fails the same way), but it says nothing about the account or the CLI (2026-10-13: tetcu72, fgovn and tetnu answered on every sandboxed invocation while `pi-cli-` and `codex-cli-bypass-fgovn` died on `EROFS` under `local-bwrap-v1`, and the verdict read `cli-fault`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`. - **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ : }`, the key is the store key an invocation declares in `credentialStore.use` (RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)): `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's store key, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. *(Superseded by RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool): the lease now receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store, pinned or not, so an account with no store for that CLI is never leased.)* Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks///stores//` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. A copy left where the account's current layout does not read (the account directory after the account moved to one store per CLI, `stores/` after it went back to one store or dropped that CLI, or an account the inventory no longer lists) is never applied, moved to the new layout or dropped: when the machine-global inventory was read, the check fails on it at any age (a torn copy and an over-limit pending directory there included) and names that directory for hand recovery; when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator, the check fails instead, names the reason (an error class and the config path, never the parser's own text), lists every retained copy at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch, since a dispatch could not run on that config either. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each confined invocation that reads a store against the store it names (RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)). An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. The same store directory also holds `torn/` (a login store a probe left half-written, kept for hand recovery and never applied or dropped), and a crash during staging can leave `pending/.tmp--`: `credential-copies-retained` reports it once its writer process is gone and it has not changed for ten minutes, and `fgos doctor --fix` removes one only after claiming it by rename (so a writer that is still running loses its own rename and keeps its home) and only when it is empty, has the same files as a copy the store keeps in `pending/` or `torn/` (the shared-memory index aside), or, under the account lock, the source login of the account shows it is no newer or it is malformed; never by age, and any other stays for hand recovery. A staging in a store the account's layout no longer reads is reported once with the stranded copies and is never touched. The doctor check and fix also read the `tempRoot` and `privateHomeRoot` a registered backend declares (absolute, without duplicates) for kept homes; the orphan reaper, the dispatch retries and the root-mode tightening stay on the default temp root, since they delete and re-mode what they find. Nothing retries a kept home under a scan-only root by itself, so doctor treats one as held at once (a failure naming the path) and `--fix` settles it by the same rule as any held home. Not built: per-CLI stores for an unconfined invocation, which keeps naming its store through its own env. - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](../../../seat-binding/spec.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **RUL82 (`RunResult.confinement` names the backend that ran, 2026-10-14).** The field was always `null`: settlement compared the requested mode with `'confined'`, a mode that does not exist (`CONFINEMENT_MODES` is `required`/`preferred`/`unconfined`), and the Assignment's confinement requirement never reached settlement. Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active. - **RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order and its cell entries; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine are per pool; a missing cell refuses by name, 2026-10-20).** Owner decisions 2026-10-19 (plan `261019-2312-model-pool-b1-fallback-and-account-order`), the walk of RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)'s cells made real. **Candidates.** `bind()` expands each `prefer` executor into one candidate per entry of its family's cell at the seat's tier (RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)), in cell order: `{ executor, invocation, pool, model }`; an entry without `@` is the family-named pool. `provenance.model.source` reads `modelPolicies..[]` (it read `resolveTierModel(.)`). `resolveTierModel` is the model of the cell's first entry whichever pool serves it (the legacy dispatch path, the runner dry-run and doctor name that model; it no longer refuses a cell that names only other pools), and `supportsPolicyTier` is true for any cell with an entry. A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](../../../seat-binding/spec.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** - **`verify` stays on the Unit.** `validateUnit` keeps `verify` (a non-empty shell command) and `skills` (a non-empty list of skill names, trimmed, de-duplicated) through validation, the units-file loader, the workflow template and the round; a registered workflow template may set both too. - **Where the verify command comes from.** `verifyCommandOf` (`patterns/reviewed.mjs`) reads the Unit's own `verify`, else its capability's `verify`, and nothing else; the `code-change` preset pins none (it used to name `npm test`, which no runner ever executed, so a reviewed run recorded a verify pass that checked nothing), and `params.verify` no longer counts. A reviewed run with no verify command still passes on its checkers but its result carries `verify: { ran: false, reason }`; a solo or panel run, which has no verify step, says nothing. - **One bounded runner.** The verify step runs through `runCommand` (`src/runner/goal-check.mjs`, the same runner `return` and `approve` use) in the Unit's worktree, for at most `runner.timeoutMs` (the existing key and default; no new key, so nothing new for setup or doctor to register). A non-zero exit, a command that could not start and one that ran past the limit are each a failed verify that becomes findings naming the status (`exited N`, `timed out after Nms`, `could not run`) and the last twenty lines of output; none of them hangs the run. - **One-liner flags.** `fgos run "" --input , --verify ""` set the Unit's `inputs` and `verify`; both are refused beside `--unit` or `--resume`, and an empty value is refused before any unit run exists. - **Skills reach `bind()`.** `bind()` skips an executor whose `supports.skills` (new optional key in the executor's `supports` block, a non-empty array of names) does not list every skill the Unit names; none left refuses with reason `skills-unavailable` naming the missing skills, and the session lead never takes over such a Unit inline. Only roles that do the Unit's work are asked for skills: checker, panel and debate roles (`reviewer`, `red-team`, `tester`, `panelist*`, `synthesizer`, `thesis`, `antithesis`, `judge`) are chosen on independence alone. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. `fgos doctor` check `executor-skills-installed` fails when a declared skill has no `SKILL.md` in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout (by each invocation's CLI: `claude` reads `.claude/skills/`, `codex` `.agents/skills/`, `omp` `.omp/skills/`, `pi` `.pi/skills/`, `grok` `.grok/skills/`, and an executor passes only when every invocation's directory has the skill; `ak:cook` is the directory `ak-cook`); `worktreeSetup.commands` copies the untracked `ak-*` skill directories from the main checkout into each new worktree, so a worker sees them. `fgos worktree create` records what its provisioning placed (`provisionWorktree` in `src/runner/worktree.mjs`: every new untracked or ignored path, with a content digest for a file and the target for a symlink, and the `node_modules` it installed declared regenerable) in `/worktree-provisioning/.json`, bound to the checkout directory's device and inode. `fgos worktree remove` moves exactly those bytes into a sibling directory before the Git port's clean check (`setProvisionedAside`): a copy only while it still matches its digest, and a recorded directory only once it is empty. It moves them back when the port refuses and deletes them, with the record, once the port has removed the checkout. A worker-edited copy or any byte the record does not name stays in place, and the port refuses on it. The brief for an `ak:cook` worker is `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md`. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11). - **`debate`: two sides soft, the judge hard.** `runDebate` (`patterns/debate.mjs`) dispatches `thesis` and `antithesis` read-only with `preferIndependentOf` each other (a shared family is reported, not refused), optionally a second round where each side gets only the other's round-1 result in `inputs`, then `judge` with `independentOf: [thesis, antithesis]` and every result as `inputs`. The judge's family differing from both sides is the one hard independence rule of the pattern; an unseatable judge is bind()'s named `independence` refusal (`policy-refusal` outcome), never a same-family ruling. The three roles are listed once, in `CHECKER_ROLES` of `bind.mjs`, so they never run inline or in-process and are not asked for the Unit's skills. `fgos doctor`'s pool-independence check drives the same pattern code, so a pool with too few families fails it before a run. `unit-summary` gives the sides seat kind `producer` and the judge `judge`.
