- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). The worker config is the repo's `.fgos/config.json` (snapshotted into `unit.json`): `fgos-runner` has no `--config` any more. Outcomes map onto the recovery matrix (`src/runner/recovery.mjs`): a failed runner commit, or an index staged before launch, is `worktree-fail`; a timeout `worker-timeout`; a command that cannot start `worker-spawn-fail`; every candidate at its provider limit `provider-limit` (park); a refusal before any worker started `no-executor` (park, the message names `runner.capabilities[""].prefer`), so one capability without a runnable pool never halts the runner; a round that ran, did not pass and left uncommitted files `worker-failed` (retry), so goal-check never judges files that are not on the branch; a round that did not pass and left nothing resolves with `commit: none` and goal-check decides on the branch as it stands. A round that stopped over its own partial writes (RUL92 (a writing seat is not run again over its own partial writes after a provider limit)) or whose runner commit failed keeps its worktree: the loop notes `{unitRunId, worktree}` under `.fgos/runtime/runner-resume/.json`, and the item's next attempt (a retry, or a later dispatch once the item is back at `todo`) resumes that same Unit run there, so a failed commit is committed again without spawning the agent; the note is checked against `unit.json` (same Unit id, worktree still checked out on `fgw/`) and dropped once the run no longer needs it. The Unit's rigor comes from the operation, then the item's `rigor`, with `risk: heavy` read as `high` only when no `rigor` is declared; bind's floor raises `low` to `standard`. The item's `refs` and `docsRef` enter the Unit only as safe repo-relative paths (others are dropped with a warning that reaches the loop log), and its `prefer` names the step's executor only when that executor is registered. The executor dispatch event carries `unitRunId`; the item log names the run the moment it exists and where its output is captured (`protected/capture/` while it runs, `stdout.log` once it settles), since a Unit run streams nothing back; a write into the main checkout during the round reaches the loop log as a `stray-write-correlated` warning. A pane run's `stdout.log` holds the settled report's text, so a worker run in a pane must put its `fgos-verdict`/`fgos-discovered` fences in its report; the loop reads the first non-empty of report, `stdout.log` and claim summary, never several. The startup reap keeps a 0-commit `fgw/` branch that a killed round still has checked out, with its uncommitted work, instead of failing on the branch delete. Not done: the loop does not resume a Unit run left `running` by a killed runner (the run id is in the item log; `fgos run --resume `); a worker detached from a killed runner may outlive it; a commit subject falls back to `producer changes` when the worker wrote no claim. - **RUL94 (a Work driver step runs as a Unit: the step's declared operation, pinned inputs, and a verdict bound to their bytes, 2026-10-14; ends the `operation-choice.mjs` entry of `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` from RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed)).** A driver step of a work item (`fgos plan --validate`, the runner loop's validate-plan and secondary operations) is built by `workUnitFor` and run through `runUnit`, never by `executeAssignment` (`src/runner/operation-choice.mjs`). `runUnit` takes `declared: {workId, domain, workflow, stage, operation, operations}` (the step's operation objects), `pinInputs` (absolute paths) and `runnerConfig` (the config the caller resolved, snapshotted instead of `.fgos/config.json`, so one step reads one config); `declared` and `pinInputs` are kept in `unit.json` and a resume reads them, and the pattern, from there. Refused before the unit directory exists: an operation the step does not declare, a `human-only` one, a stamped mutation that disagrees with the unit's `writes` (read-only exactly when it writes nothing), and any pattern that does not resolve to `solo`. Only the producer seat carries the operation: its assignment has the operation's role and normalizer stamp (`mutation`, `evidence`, `resultKind`, `onAdvance`, built by `declaredOperationFields` in `src/runner/dispatch/assignment.mjs`, shared with `buildAssignment`), the seat name stays in `provenance.role`, and `policy.rigor` is the unit's rigor. At launch the dispatch hashes each pin into `inputDigests[{path, root, rel, sha256}]` in `run.json` and `result.json`; a pin is read only when its real path lies in the main checkout or a worktree git lists (not one that became a symlink), against the innermost such root, else its `sha256` is `null` and nothing is read. The verdict walker (`findLatestAssignmentRunResult`) reads flat and nested layouts through `listAssignmentRuns`, filters by `operation`, takes only a unit run's producer seat, and compares the current `plan.md` by `rel` and digest; a pinned digest decides alone (no mtime pre-filter), so a plan merged byte for byte into another checkout still matches, and `planContentHash` is only read on results from before this rule. The driver hands the producer's own RunResult and seat assignment to `interpretAssignmentRunResult`, stops on a unit with no result or whose runner commit failed (`unit-commit-failed`), and never turns an item ref naming another run's output (`unit-run:`, `gate-answer:`) into an input. The worker is confined (`session: {headless: true, herdrPresent: false}`): a read-only operation cannot write the checkout, and a machine with no confinement backend stops the step (`unit-refused-posture-unavailable`). A unit with `rigor: low` is raised to `standard` by bind's floor. Not done here: a pin resolved through `process.cwd()` first (`resolveContentRoot`) can differ from the plan in the item worktree a secondary operation runs in. - **RUL95 (dispatch takes generic inputs only; Work is a consumer, 2026-10-14; decision 0063, replaces the input part of RUL73 (dispatch does not know Work).2 and closes the `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` list of RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed)).** `src/runner/dispatch/**`, `src/runner/execution/**`, `src/runner/dispatch.mjs` and `src/workflow/**` never handle a Work item. Rigor and domain are the assignment's own fields: `resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy` reads `assignment.rigor` where it read `work.rigor`/`work.risk` (first explicit source may pick it, after an operation rigor it only raises, the capability floor and tier rules are unchanged; provenance scope `assignment`) and `assignment.domain` for the `:review` capability floor, so a declared Unit step (whose seat carries `domain`) gets that floor again. The Work layer folds an item's `rigor` and `risk: heavy` into one rigor (`workRigorFor`). `decide --work` gets a hint from the Work layer, `workDispatchHint`/`resolveWorkForDispatch` → `{workExecutorId, agentType, rigor?, domain?}`, passed to `compileDispatchPlan({workId, workHint})`; fan-out uses the same hint. `workDispatchContext` returns only `{capabilityHints, agentType}`. `buildAssignment`, `resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`, `compileDispatchPlan`, `decideExecutorCli`, `executeExecutorCli` and `executeAssignment` refuse a `work`, `workItem` or `workExecutorId` input (`RunnerConfigError` "takes no Work item") instead of ignoring it; `decideExecutorCli` and `compileDispatchPlan` name the `--work` selector `workId`. `executeExecutorCli` no longer runs an unregistered executor id because a Work item rode along (`executor-not-found`). A domain's contract harness (ADR-007) is loaded only by the Work layer (`domainHarnessFor(work, {domain})`, only for a registered domain at a declared step; `loadHarnessModule` treats a module that fails to import as no harness), and a caller hands it to the inline `buildAssignment` as `options.domainHarness`; dispatch still re-validates the enriched contract and records `domain-harness-seam`. No production path builds an inline assignment for a Work item today (none did before either: the only inline caller is `probe-account`), so the seam runs only in tests. The guard (`test/architecture.test.mjs`) refuses, outside comments and other string text, any identifier or property named `work`, `workItem` or `docsRef` (identifier escapes such as `\u0077ork` are decoded first), any string that is exactly one of those names (a computed or quoted key, `Reflect.get(o, 'work')`, a key comparison; only the pinned uses are allowed: the `--work` selector's type in `plan.mjs` and the refused option names in `assignment-policy.mjs`), and any `resolveContentRoot(` call in the guarded files; `src/state/**` counts as Work layer for the transitive import guard, except one pinned edge (`worktree.mjs` takes only `StoreError` from `src/state/store.mjs`); imports are read with optional whitespace, comments blanked, `?query` dropped, and absolute paths and `file:` URLs resolved; the guarded folders may hold only plain `.mjs` files (no `.js`/`.cjs`/TypeScript source, no symlink); the shared source lexer treats a slash after a block's closing brace as a regular expression, so its quotes cannot hide the code after it; it also refuses an `import()`/`require()` whose specifier is not one plain literal, `createRequire`, `eval`, `Function(...)` (with or without `new`) and an import of `module`, `vm` or `worker_threads` (with or without `node:`), except the loads pinned one by one in a named allowlist entry with its reason (`provider-credential-renewal.mjs`: `createRequire` for `node:sqlite`); one more load in an allowlisted file fails too. The call-site guard also counts a string that is exactly a door's name (`d['executeAssignment'](a)`) and an escaped name as a use, and compares each run door with exactly its named callers (`executeAssignment`: `execution/run.mjs`, `dispatch/cli.mjs`; `executeExecutorCli`: `dispatch/assignment-runner.mjs`; `commitUnitWork`: `execution/run.mjs`; `executeThroughConfinement`: `dispatch/cli.mjs`), both ways. Not covered: a name built at run time (`opts[k]`, `opts['wo' + 'rk']`, `globalThis['ev' + 'al']`), nested inputs (`options.work`, `assignment.work`; nothing reads them), and code outside the guarded files that reaches into dispatch's internals. - **RUL96 (one run may take its own timeout, from 1m to 4h; its private home and worktree lock last as long, 2026-10-15).** A unit run's seats are dispatched with `runner.timeoutMs` unless the run asks for its own: `fgos run --timeout ` (a whole number and one unit, `ms|s|m|h`: `90m`, `5400s`), a `timeoutMs` key on an `--override` object (`--timeout` adds it to every override that names none, and an unscoped one when none is unscoped, as `--effort` does), or a Unit's `timeoutMs` (whole milliseconds; a units file and a Workflow unit template carry it too, a template's value is checked when the definition loads). `bind()` resolves override, then unit, into `binding.timeoutMs` with `provenance.timeoutMs { value, source: override: | unit | none }`; a value outside the range is a refused binding (`run-timeout`), and an override's value is checked before the unit run exists. The value lives in `unit.json` (`overrides`, `unit`, and every recorded binding), so a resume dispatches with it and `--timeout` is refused with `--resume`; `runUnit` hands it to `executeAssignment` (`opts.timeoutMs ?? cfg.timeoutMs`), which already threads it to the worker kill, the pane poll and the dispatch lock. Range (`src/runner/dispatch/run-timeout.mjs`): the 1m floor keeps a typo (`90s` for `90m`) from killing a turn at once; the 4h ceiling, four times the heaviest turn seen, bounds how long a hung worker holds its worktree's lock and a copy of an account login, and `runner.timeoutMs` above it is refused when the config loads, so the default obeys it too. The confinement reaper keeps a home whose dispatcher pid is alive and has no pane until `createdAt + max(maxAgeMs, min(marker.timeoutMs, 4h) + 10m)` (the bwrap driver records the dispatch's `timeoutMs` in the ownership marker; a marker without one keeps the 1h rule; a dead dispatcher's home goes at once, a pane-retained home is unchanged), so a pane-less run longer than an hour is no longer reaped mid-turn. The per-worktree dispatch lock is a kernel lock with no ttl (RUL101 (the per-worktree dispatch lock is a kernel lock)): a dead holder releases it at once, and a live holder holds it until it exits, so a live but wedged dispatcher blocks its worktree with no time limit while the worker it started is still killed at the run timeout. `--override` passed with `--resume` is ignored, as for every override key (the run keeps `unit.json#overrides`). - **RUL97 (a Unit may sync a base ref first: the runner merges it, the worker only edits the conflicted files, 2026-10-15).** A Unit may carry `syncBase` (a branch, tag or commit name: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `/`, `-`, not starting with `-` or `/`, no `..`); it needs `writes` and a linked worktree, and `fgos run --sync ` sets it (with a prompt: sync, then the task; without one: a sync-only Unit, `syncOnly: true`, whose objective is `Merge into this branch.`). The ref is resolved to a commit once, before the unit run exists (a ref naming no commit, or a run from the main checkout, leaves nothing behind), and `unit.json#sync` keeps `{ ref, sha, status, head?, conflicts?, mergeStaged?, commit? }`; a resume merges that sha, never the ref again. Before any seat runs, the runner merges it with the trusted git of RUL85 (the runner commits only the Unit's write scope) — `merge --no-commit --no-ff`, rerere and autostash off — in `src/runner/execution/commit-unit-work.mjs` (`startSyncMerge`, `finishSyncMerge`, `syncMergeState`), orchestrated by `src/runner/execution/unit-sync.mjs`: already in the branch is `up-to-date`; a clean merge is committed by the runner as `chore(sync): merge ` (status `merged`; a commit that is not the merge of `sha` over `head` holding exactly what the merge staged — a hook added a file — fails `committed-set-mismatch` as `execution-failure`, stays on the branch, and the resume is refused until a person takes it off) and the Unit goes on to its pattern, or passes at once when sync-only; a sync never brings the base side of `.fgos/` in: every `.fgos/**` path the merge staged or left conflicted, clean or not, is put back to the branch side (HEAD), a path the base deleted is kept and a path only the base has is not taken — ADR0020 (a worker branch never commits `.fgos/`), the side `fgos-write-rejected` at approve resolves to the target for a `.fgos/` path the branch left unchanged, on every branch, not only `fgw/*`; any other conflict leaves the merge open (status `conflicted`), puts the conflicted paths the scope does not already cover in scope only while the merge is open (`sync.scopeAdded`, read by the effective scope only while `sync.status === 'conflicted'`; `writeScope` itself stays as declared, so a later round cannot write them), and appends a `## Merge to finish` section to the writing seat's brief naming them and telling it never to run git. A refused start leaves no merge open and ends the run: `merge-in-progress` (a merge someone else opened), `foreign-staged-index`, `merge-refused` (git would not start, e.g. a dirty file it would overwrite), `hook-refused` (the pre-commit hook of the main checkout's hooks path refused the clean merge commit; told apart from a git failure by running that hook once more as git runs it, and its words are the detail), `unscopable-conflict-path` (a conflicted path the scope normalizer of RUL84 (one write-scope matcher) would read differently — `*`, a leading `:`, `\`, surrounding whitespace — or holding a control character, since it is also printed into the brief; the merge is aborted) as `policy-refusal`, and `git-error` as `execution-failure`. While the merge is open, the preflight of a writing seat counts only the open MERGE_HEAD equal to `sync.sha` over `sync.head` as the run's own: its conflicted and merge-staged paths are neither a foreign index nor `preExistingInScope`; any other open merge refuses a writing seat (`merge-in-progress`) and `commitUnitWork` never commits over one. After a passing round the runner concludes the merge before the round's own commit: a conflicted file that still holds a line opening with seven or more `<`, `|` or `>` (a larger `conflict-marker-size` included; a file holding a NUL byte is read as binary and not checked) fails the commit `conflict-markers` with `paths`, stages nothing and keeps the merge, so `fgos run --resume` only commits once a person removed them (RUL86 (`fgos run --resume` after a failed runner commit only commits)); otherwise it stages the conflicted paths, refuses an index holding anything the merge did not stage (`staged-set-mismatch`, taking back what it staged itself, e.g. a conflicted file the worker turned into a directory), commits with MERGE_HEAD as second parent (a refusing pre-commit hook fails it `hook-refused` with the hook's words and keeps the merge; each `fgos run --resume` tries the commit once, never in a loop), checks parents and committed set (`committed-set-mismatch`), and then commits the rest of the round inside the scope as usual. The round's `commit` carries the merge's own record under `sync`; `runUnit` returns `sync` beside `outcome`; a sync-only unit that needed no worker returns one result `{ role: 'sync', round: 0, commit }` (no `verify`, as for `solo`). A round that did not pass keeps the merge open; a resume checks it first: still open, it runs the seat again over it; concluded by hand (its sha in the branch), it is `merged`; aborted, or HEAD moved, the resume is refused and names the merge. A run that died between starting git and recording the result adopts its own open merge on resume; a first start never adopts one. A resumed sync-only run that was `up-to-date` or `merged` passes again without a worker. Settlement: the writing seat over an open merge carries `assignment.syncConflicts`; those files, dirty at launch, changed during the turn and inside its scope, count as its evidence (`evidence.editedSyncConflicts`), so a seat that only resolves conflicts is not scored `verdict-inconclusive`. Any other file dirty at launch that a seat rewrites still is no evidence, with or without a sync. A units file (`fgos workflow start --units`) naming `syncBase` is refused: a workflow unit's worktree starts from its dependency's branch, and a sync there is not built. Not done: an inline producer over an open merge (inline rounds have no runner commit), a modify/delete conflict whose worker deletes the file is concluded as a deletion. - **RUL98 (`fgos workflow start` kế thừa và phân bổ `--timeout ` và `--account ` cho từng Unit, 2026-10-15).** Workflow run hỗ trợ cờ `--timeout ` (chuỗi thời lượng hợp lệ `1m`..`4h`, phân tích ra `timeoutMs`) và `--account ` (ghim tài khoản nhà cung cấp) giống cơ chế của `--effort`. Cả hai giá trị được lưu bền vững trong payload của sự kiện `workflow.start` và được tái tạo khi `resume`. Về thứ tự ưu tiên timeout: cờ `--timeout` của `fgos run` THẮNG `unit.timeoutMs` của Unit (RUL96 (one run may take its own timeout, from 1m to 4h): override thắng unit), trong khi `--timeout` của `fgos workflow start` NHƯỜNG cho `unit.timeoutMs` tự khai của Unit. Về account: `--account` của workflow chỉ ghim cho các seat thuộc provider sở hữu account đó; các Unit không có seat nào khớp sẽ chạy bình thường không ghim và không làm hỏng workflow; `--account` không tồn tại trong bất kỳ `runner.providers.*.accounts` nào sẽ bị từ chối ngay lúc start trước khi tạo run. - **RUL99 (Bảng mã thoát riêng biệt cho kết cục thực thi của `fgos run` và `fgos workflow start|resume|answer --foreground`, 2026-10-15).** Các outcome kết thúc không phải `pass` của `fgos run` và `fgos workflow start|resume|answer --foreground` chuyển sang sử dụng bảng exit code xác định: `pass` = 0, `policy-refusal` = 4 (validation), `provider-limit` = 10, `execution-failure` = 11, `partial-writes` = 12, `blocked` = 13, `findings` = 14. Các lệnh chỉ-đọc như `fgos workflow status` luôn trả về mã thoát 0 bất kể outcome của workflow run. Lệnh `fgos workflow start` ở chế độ detached vẫn trả về mã 0 khi tiến trình daemon được khởi chạy thành công. Định dạng envelope JSON stdout `fgos.v1` giữ nguyên vẹn 100%. - **RUL100 (Doctor check `executor-posture-coverage` chẩn đoán posture readiness của các executor, 2026-10-15).** Check doctor `executor-posture-coverage` kiểm tra tĩnh khả năng áp dụng posture cho các core capabilities (`execute`, `code:implement`) và mọi capability khai báo pool agent (`prefer`). Quá trình kiểm tra chạy hoàn toàn khô qua `bind()`, không spawn tiến trình, không tạo pane herdr, không kích hoạt sandbox. Khi một capability có executor thiếu sandbox bwrap, check báo lỗi `posture-unavailable` (`passed: false`). Khi một capability thiếu pool (`headless-no-executor` / `no-candidate`), check chỉ phát cảnh báo (`passed: true`, tiền tố `warning:`) hướng dẫn khai báo `runner.capabilities..prefer`.

placement.content:
- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. Only roles that do the Unit's work are asked for skills: checker, panel and debate roles (`reviewer`, `red-team`, `tester`, `panelist*`, `synthesizer`, `thesis`, `antithesis`, `judge`) are chosen on independence alone. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. `fgos doctor` check `executor-skills-installed` fails when a declared skill has no `SKILL.md` in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout (by each invocation's CLI: `claude` reads `.claude/skills/`, `codex` `.agents/skills/`, `omp` `.omp/skills/`, `pi` `.pi/skills/`, `grok` `.grok/skills/`, and an executor passes only when every invocation's directory has the skill; `ak:cook` is the directory `ak-cook`); `worktreeSetup.commands` copies the untracked `ak-*` skill directories from the main checkout into each new worktree, so a worker sees them. `fgos worktree create` records what its provisioning placed (`provisionWorktree` in `src/runner/worktree.mjs`: every new untracked or ignored path, with a content digest for a file and the target for a symlink, and the `node_modules` it installed declared regenerable) in `/worktree-provisioning/.json`, bound to the checkout directory's device and inode. `fgos worktree remove` moves exactly those bytes into a sibling directory before the Git port's clean check (`setProvisionedAside`): a copy only while it still matches its digest, and a recorded directory only once it is empty. It moves them back when the port refuses and deletes them, with the record, once the port has removed the checkout. A worker-edited copy or any byte the record does not name stays in place, and the port refuses on it. The brief for an `ak:cook` worker is `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md`. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11). - **`debate`: two sides soft, the judge hard.** `runDebate` (`patterns/debate.mjs`) dispatches `thesis` and `antithesis` read-only with `preferIndependentOf` each other (a shared family is reported, not refused), optionally a second round where each side gets only the other's round-1 result in `inputs`, then `judge` with `independentOf: [thesis, antithesis]` and every result as `inputs`. The judge's family differing from both sides is the one hard independence rule of the pattern; an unseatable judge is bind()'s named `independence` refusal (`policy-refusal` outcome), never a same-family ruling. The three roles are listed once, in `CHECKER_ROLES` of `bind.mjs`, so they never run inline or in-process and are not asked for the Unit's skills. `fgos doctor`'s pool-independence check drives the same pattern code, so a pool with too few families fails it before a run. `unit-summary` gives the sides seat kind `producer` and the judge `judge`.

- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). Range (`src/runner/dispatch/run-timeout.mjs`): the 1m floor keeps a typo (`90s` for `90m`) from killing a turn at once; the 4h ceiling, four times the heaviest turn seen, bounds how long a hung worker holds its worktree's lock and a copy of an account login, and `runner.timeoutMs` above it is refused when the config loads, so the default obeys it too. The confinement reaper keeps a home whose dispatcher pid is alive and has no pane until `createdAt + max(maxAgeMs, min(marker.timeoutMs, 4h) + 10m)` (the bwrap driver records the dispatch's `timeoutMs` in the ownership marker; a marker without one keeps the 1h rule; a dead dispatcher's home goes at once, a pane-retained home is unchanged), so a pane-less run longer than an hour is no longer reaped mid-turn. The per-worktree dispatch lock is a kernel lock with no ttl (RUL101 (the per-worktree dispatch lock is a kernel lock)): a dead holder releases it at once, and a live holder holds it until it exits, so a live but wedged dispatcher blocks its worktree with no time limit while the worker it started is still killed at the run timeout. `--override` passed with `--resume` is ignored, as for every override key (the run keeps `unit.json#overrides`). - **RUL97 (a Unit may sync a base ref first: the runner merges it, the worker only edits the conflicted files, 2026-10-15).** A Unit may carry `syncBase` (a branch, tag or commit name: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `/`, `-`, not starting with `-` or `/`, no `..`); it needs `writes` and a linked worktree, and `fgos run --sync ` sets it (with a prompt: sync, then the task; without one: a sync-only Unit, `syncOnly: true`, whose objective is `Merge into this branch.`). The ref is resolved to a commit once, before the unit run exists (a ref naming no commit, or a run from the main checkout, leaves nothing behind), and `unit.json#sync` keeps `{ ref, sha, status, head?, conflicts?, mergeStaged?, commit? }`; a resume merges that sha, never the ref again. Before any seat runs, the runner merges it with the trusted git of RUL85 (the runner commits only the Unit's write scope) — `merge --no-commit --no-ff`, rerere and autostash off — in `src/runner/execution/commit-unit-work.mjs` (`startSyncMerge`, `finishSyncMerge`, `syncMergeState`), orchestrated by `src/runner/execution/unit-sync.mjs`: already in the branch is `up-to-date`; a clean merge is committed by the runner as `chore(sync): merge ` (status `merged`; a commit that is not the merge of `sha` over `head` holding exactly what the merge staged — a hook added a file — fails `committed-set-mismatch` as `execution-failure`, stays on the branch, and the resume is refused until a person takes it off) and the Unit goes on to its pattern, or passes at once when sync-only; a sync never brings the base side of `.fgos/` in: every `.fgos/**` path the merge staged or left conflicted, clean or not, is put back to the branch side (HEAD), a path the base deleted is kept and a path only the base has is not taken — ADR0020 (a worker branch never commits `.fgos/`), the side `fgos-write-rejected` at approve resolves to the target for a `.fgos/` path the branch left unchanged, on every branch, not only `fgw/*`; any other conflict leaves the merge open (status `conflicted`), puts the conflicted paths the scope does not already cover in scope only while the merge is open (`sync.scopeAdded`, read by the effective scope only while `sync.status === 'conflicted'`; `writeScope` itself stays as declared, so a later round cannot write them), and appends a `## Merge to finish` section to the writing seat's brief naming them and telling it never to run git. A refused start leaves no merge open and ends the run: `merge-in-progress` (a merge someone else opened), `foreign-staged-index`, `merge-refused` (git would not start, e.g. a dirty file it would overwrite), `hook-refused` (the pre-commit hook of the main checkout's hooks path refused the clean merge commit; told apart from a git failure by running that hook once more as git runs it, and its words are the detail), `unscopable-conflict-path` (a conflicted path the scope normalizer of RUL84 (one write-scope matcher) would read differently — `*`, a leading `:`, `\`, surrounding whitespace — or holding a control character, since it is also printed into the brief; the merge is aborted) as `policy-refusal`, and `git-error` as `execution-failure`. While the merge is open, the preflight of a writing seat counts only the open MERGE_HEAD equal to `sync.sha` over `sync.head` as the run's own: its conflicted and merge-staged paths are neither a foreign index nor `preExistingInScope`; any other open merge refuses a writing seat (`merge-in-progress`) and `commitUnitWork` never commits over one. After a passing round the runner concludes the merge before the round's own commit: a conflicted file that still holds a line opening with seven or more `<`, `|` or `>` (a larger `conflict-marker-size` included; a file holding a NUL byte is read as binary and not checked) fails the commit `conflict-markers` with `paths`, stages nothing and keeps the merge, so `fgos run --resume` only commits once a person removed them (RUL86 (`fgos run --resume` after a failed runner commit only commits)); otherwise it stages the conflicted paths, refuses an index holding anything the merge did not stage (`staged-set-mismatch`, taking back what it staged itself, e.g. a conflicted file the worker turned into a directory), commits with MERGE_HEAD as second parent (a refusing pre-commit hook fails it `hook-refused` with the hook's words and keeps the merge; each `fgos run --resume` tries the commit once, never in a loop), checks parents and committed set (`committed-set-mismatch`), and then commits the rest of the round inside the scope as usual. The round's `commit` carries the merge's own record under `sync`; `runUnit` returns `sync` beside `outcome`; a sync-only unit that needed no worker returns one result `{ role: 'sync', round: 0, commit }` (no `verify`, as for `solo`). A round that did not pass keeps the merge open; a resume checks it first: still open, it runs the seat again over it; concluded by hand (its sha in the branch), it is `merged`; aborted, or HEAD moved, the resume is refused and names the merge. A run that died between starting git and recording the result adopts its own open merge on resume; a first start never adopts one. A resumed sync-only run that was `up-to-date` or `merged` passes again without a worker. Settlement: the writing seat over an open merge carries `assignment.syncConflicts`; those files, dirty at launch, changed during the turn and inside its scope, count as its evidence (`evidence.editedSyncConflicts`), so a seat that only resolves conflicts is not scored `verdict-inconclusive`. Any other file dirty at launch that a seat rewrites still is no evidence, with or without a sync. A units file (`fgos workflow start --units`) naming `syncBase` is refused: a workflow unit's worktree starts from its dependency's branch, and a sync there is not built. Not done: an inline producer over an open merge (inline rounds have no runner commit), a modify/delete conflict whose worker deletes the file is concluded as a deletion. - **RUL98 (`fgos workflow start` kế thừa và phân bổ `--timeout ` và `--account ` cho từng Unit, 2026-10-15).** Workflow run hỗ trợ cờ `--timeout ` (chuỗi thời lượng hợp lệ `1m`..`4h`, phân tích ra `timeoutMs`) và `--account ` (ghim tài khoản nhà cung cấp) giống cơ chế của `--effort`. Cả hai giá trị được lưu bền vững trong payload của sự kiện `workflow.start` và được tái tạo khi `resume`. Về thứ tự ưu tiên timeout: cờ `--timeout` của `fgos run` THẮNG `unit.timeoutMs` của Unit (RUL96 (one run may take its own timeout, from 1m to 4h): override thắng unit), trong khi `--timeout` của `fgos workflow start` NHƯỜNG cho `unit.timeoutMs` tự khai của Unit. Về account: `--account` của workflow chỉ ghim cho các seat thuộc provider sở hữu account đó; các Unit không có seat nào khớp sẽ chạy bình thường không ghim và không làm hỏng workflow; `--account` không tồn tại trong bất kỳ `runner.providers.*.accounts` nào sẽ bị từ chối ngay lúc start trước khi tạo run. - **RUL99 (Bảng mã thoát riêng biệt cho kết cục thực thi của `fgos run` và `fgos workflow start|resume|answer --foreground`, 2026-10-15).** Các outcome kết thúc không phải `pass` của `fgos run` và `fgos workflow start|resume|answer --foreground` chuyển sang sử dụng bảng exit code xác định: `pass` = 0, `policy-refusal` = 4 (validation), `provider-limit` = 10, `execution-failure` = 11, `partial-writes` = 12, `blocked` = 13, `findings` = 14. Các lệnh chỉ-đọc như `fgos workflow status` luôn trả về mã thoát 0 bất kể outcome của workflow run. Lệnh `fgos workflow start` ở chế độ detached vẫn trả về mã 0 khi tiến trình daemon được khởi chạy thành công. Định dạng envelope JSON stdout `fgos.v1` giữ nguyên vẹn 100%. - **RUL100 (Doctor check `executor-posture-coverage` chẩn đoán posture readiness của các executor, 2026-10-15).** Check doctor `executor-posture-coverage` kiểm tra tĩnh khả năng áp dụng posture cho các core capabilities (`execute`, `code:implement`) và mọi capability khai báo pool agent (`prefer`). Quá trình kiểm tra chạy hoàn toàn khô qua `bind()`, không spawn tiến trình, không tạo pane herdr, không kích hoạt sandbox. Khi một capability có executor thiếu sandbox bwrap, check báo lỗi `posture-unavailable` (`passed: false`). Khi một capability thiếu pool (`headless-no-executor` / `no-candidate`), check chỉ phát cảnh báo (`passed: true`, tiền tố `warning:`) hướng dẫn khai báo `runner.capabilities..prefer`.

placement.content:
| Entry point | Status | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `install.sh` | Implemented | Installs `fgctl` from release assets into a machine-local install directory. |
| `install.ps1` | Implemented preview | The Windows counterpart of `install.sh` (PowerShell 5.1 or later, no administrator rights, no `PATH` change): installs `fgctl.exe` for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` with the same `FGCTL_VERSION` / `FGCTL_INSTALL_DIR` / `FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL` / `FGCTL_TARGET` semantics and a mandatory `SHA256SUMS` check (rule RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell) in `docs/specs/distribution.md`). |
| `fgctl init` | Implemented preview | Initializes a project/workspace from a release chosen by `--from` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION` > the committed pin > the latest GitHub release; a downloaded asset is checksum-verified against `SHA256SUMS` before staging (rule RUL15 (fgctl init downloads a checksum-verified release when no source is given) in `docs/specs/distribution.md`). |
| `fgos` launcher | Implemented preview | One `fgos` (`fgos.cmd` on Windows) written next to `fgctl` by `fgos doctor --fix` (which `fgctl init` runs): it walks up to the nearest `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos` and runs it, so each project runs its own activated release with no absolute path and no rc edit. A different `fgos` found first on `PATH` is reported, never overwritten. See distribution spec RUL17 (one fgos on PATH runs each project's own activated fgos). |
| `fgctl upgrade` | Implemented preview | Moves a workspace activation to a new release chosen by `--from` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION` > the latest GitHub release (checksum-verified against `SHA256SUMS` when downloaded), records the previous release for rollback, and updates `.fgos/distribution.json` (including `releaseVersion` when downloaded). |
| `fgctl repair` | Implemented preview | Repairs a workspace installation under the selected release model; current preview proof covers repair after activation. |
| `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos` | Implemented preview | Stable workspace command surface after activation; current preview proof reports `host: "rust"` and the activated `artifactDigest`. |
| `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos.cmd`, `fgos-runner.cmd` | Implemented preview | The same stable surface for PowerShell and `cmd.exe`, written by `fgctl init`/`repair` next to the `sh` pair and needing no POSIX shell; `fgctl verify` reports a missing or edited launcher and `fgctl repair` regenerates it. |
| `npm install -g github:vantt/forgent` | Implemented legacy deprecated | Installs the legacy Node `fgos` and `fgos-runner` entry points; explicit deprecated escape hatch during the compatibility window, not the public/default posture. |
| `scripts/fgos-shell-integration.sh` | Implemented | Contributor/dev helper that resolves fgOS command tiers from shell functions. |
| local `fgos init` | Partial target | Adopts/materializes workspace state after `fgctl` publishes a ready activation. |
| `fgos doctor` | Implemented | Reports environment checks without writing by default. |
| `fgos doctor --fix` | Implemented | Runs registered fixes and then reports checks. |
| `fgos setup` | Implemented deprecated legacy compatibility | Wires local development support and runs registered environment repairs in the current Node CLI; command surfaces point workspace onboarding to `fgctl init` plus local `fgos doctor --fix`/`fgos doctor`, while shell/global integration remains compatibility behavior through the 30-day preview fallback window unless a later release decision replaces it. |
